title: Market scanner using IBKR's scanner categories, disabled when IBKR isn't available
description: Ch. 56 describes scanning a large universe the user doesn't already track (S&P 500, an industry group, etc.) to discover new candidates -- distinct from the watchlist (a curated list of tickers already tracked) and the ticker detail view (analyzes one already-chosen ticker). Per explicit product decision: this uses IBKRProvider.run_scanner's predefined categories (52-week-high/low, hot-by-volume, top % gainers/losers, etc. -- confirmed present in get_scanner_params's option list) when the gateway is enabled and available, and the feature is simply unavailable (a clear 'scanner unavailable, IBKR not connected' state, never a hard error) otherwise. Elder's own bespoke custom-pattern scanner (a precursor-to-divergence detector built with a programmer) is explicitly NOT in scope here -- that remains a separate, much larger idea in docs/ideas.md if ever pursued; this task only wires up IBKR's own existing scan categories.

checklist.step: Add an endpoint exposing the available scanner categories (from IBKRProvider.get_scanner_params) and an endpoint to run a scan (via IBKRProvider.run_scanner), both returning a clear 'unavailable' response (not an error) when IBKR isn't enabled/available -- reuse the same gateway-availability pattern backend-ibkr-status-endpoint establishes.

Decide and record which of IBKR's scan categories to expose as the initial curated set (vs. exposing the raw params list as-is) and any default negative filters (e.g. a minimum average-daily-volume floor, per ch.56's own liquidity-filter advice) -- record the rationale.
Respect IBKRProvider's existing client-side rate limits (1 req/sec for run_scanner, 15-min cache for get_scanner_params) -- do not add a second, conflicting throttle layer.
Unit tests mocking IBKRProvider for: IBKR disabled, gateway unavailable, a successful scan, and the rate-limited case.

decisions.decision: Both routes (GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params, POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run) live in the existing backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py alongside GET /api/ibkr/status, rather than a new router file. GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params exposes IBKR's raw scan_type_list from get_scanner_params, passed through as a list[dict] as-is, rather than hand-curating a fixed subset of category codes. POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run's scan_config field is likewise an opaque dict forwarded to IBKRProvider.run_scanner without validation or a server-injected default liquidity filter (e.g. no automatic min-average-volume floor). Both routes report availability via the identical {state, detail} shape GET /api/ibkr/status already established (IBKRGatewayState: disabled/available/gateway_unreachable/not_authenticated), with categories/results populated only when state == 'available'. Being rate-limited (IBKRProvider.run_scanner's own 1-req/sec client-side throttle, IBKRRateLimitedError) is surfaced as an HTTP 429 with the exception's own message as detail, not folded into the {state} shape, since it's a genuine transient error on an otherwise-available scanner, distinct from 'IBKR isn't connected at all'.
decisions.rationale: One router per resource is this codebase's established convention (stocks.py/portfolio.py/watchlist.py, and ibkr.py itself for /status) -- the scanner routes are the same 'ibkr' resource, not a new one. Passing through the raw scan_type_list (rather than a curated subset) was chosen because the actual field shape/available codes are unconfirmed against a live gateway (docs/ideas.md's own admission: 'confirmed not yet checked against a live gateway') -- hand-picking specific category codes risks embedding stale or wrong codes, silently omitting categories IBKR actually offers, or breaking outright if the real field names differ from assumption. This mirrors IBKRProvider.run_scanner's own already-established design philosophy (its docstring: 'this provider doesn't validate scan_config itself, since the option universe is entirely gateway-defined and versioned by IBKR, not something worth duplicating here') -- the same reasoning applies one layer up at the API boundary. For the same reason, no default negative filter (e.g. a volume floor) is injected server-side: the exact IBKR filter code/schema for something like an average-daily-volume floor is unconfirmed against a live gateway, and guessing at one risks constructing a filter that's subtly wrong or silently a no-op; ch.56's liquidity-filter advice is instead documented (in the route docstrings and docs/architecture/API.md) as guidance for the caller to apply via whatever filter option IBKR's own get_scanner_params response actually offers. 429 (not a 'state' value) for rate-limiting was chosen because it's the standard, actionable HTTP status for 'you're calling too fast, retry shortly' -- collapsing it into the same {state, detail} shape used for 'feature unavailable' would blur two very different situations (a permanently-unusable feature right now vs. a fully-usable feature that just needs a brief retry) that a caller needs to handle differently. Also considered eagerly calling get_gateway_status() first in both handlers (mirroring /status exactly) before attempting get_scanner_params()/run_scanner(); rejected in favor of a try/except around the data call itself, falling back to get_gateway_status() only on an IBKRUnavailableError -- this avoids a redundant extra gateway round-trip on every successful/cached call, paying the extra status check only on the (already-failing) unavailable path where it's needed to report which specific state applies instead of parsing IBKRUnavailableError's message string.

decisions.decision: Fixed pr-reviewer's blocking finding (PR #214, both scanner routes returning state: "available" with categories/results: null) by adding a shared `_resolve_scanner_unavailable` helper: on `IBKRUnavailableError`, it makes the same fresh `get_gateway_status()` call as before, but if that fresh check itself reports `available` -- meaning the exception came from the scanner-specific call failing transiently (a non-200/transport-error/unparseable body from `/iserver/scanner/params` or `/iserver/scanner/run`), not from the gateway/session genuinely being unavailable -- it raises `HTTPException(503)` with the original exception's message as `detail`, instead of returning a `state`-shaped 200. Both routes' `responses={...}` and docs/architecture/API.md were updated to document the new `503` case, and a regression test was added on each route (`test_transient_scanner_call_failure_with_available_gateway_returns_503`) using the existing test stub's already-decoupled `status`/`*_result` fields to construct exactly the disagreeing-status-vs-exception scenario pr-reviewer reproduced.
decisions.rationale: A 503 (not a new `state` value) was chosen to match this codebase's existing 'genuine, transient, single-call failure' convention (stocks.py's DataProviderUnavailableError -> 503) and to keep it clearly distinct from both `429` (a client calling too fast, not a call that outright failed) and the `state` enum (which means 'this feature is not usable at all right now', not 'this one call to it just failed'); folding a transient scanner-call failure into `state` would have required inventing a new IBKRGatewayState value that doesn't correspond to anything `IBKRProvider.get_gateway_status()` itself can report, and would still leave the underlying ambiguity (does a caller retry, or is the whole feature down?) unresolved. Considered instead trying to distinguish the two `IBKRUnavailableError` causes by parsing its message string (`_require_available` vs `_request`'s three raise sites use different wording) or by adding a new exception subclass in `app.data.ibkr_provider` for the `_request`-only case; rejected both -- message-string parsing is brittle and exactly the kind of coupling `IBKRUnavailableError`'s own docstring already discourages, and a new provider-level exception type would touch a class three other tasks/tests already depend on for a router-only bug, when the same fresh-status-disagrees-with-exception signal this fix uses is already available at the router layer with no provider change needed. Addresses pr-reviewer's blocking comment on PR #214 (see this task's `review.comments`).

comments.summary: Blocking: GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params and POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run can return state: "available" together with categories/results left null, violating the schema's own documented "non-null iff state == 'available'" invariant. Happens when IBKRProvider's scanner-specific call itself fails transiently (a non-200 response, transport error, or unparseable body from /iserver/scanner/params or /iserver/scanner/run) while a fresh get_gateway_status() call (hitting the unrelated /iserver/auth/status endpoint) still reports 'available'. Reproduced directly against the branch: a stub with get_gateway_status() -> available and get_scanner_params() raising IBKRUnavailableError('...HTTP 500...') yields 200 {"state": "available", "categories": null} (and the mirror case for run_scanner/results). No existing test exercises this path.

Non-blocking: IBKRRateLimitedError.retry_after is discarded by the 429 response, only embedded in detail's free-text sentence rather than a structured field or Retry-After header. Tracked on backend-market-scanner-followups.

Non-blocking: the except IBKRUnavailableError fallback pattern is duplicated verbatim between get_ibkr_scanner_params and run_ibkr_scanner; worth extracting a shared helper, especially once the blocking finding there is fixed. Tracked on backend-market-scanner-followups.

Non-blocking: get_ibkr_scanner_params's isinstance(params, dict) check is redundant given the trailing `or []` already normalizes any falsy/non-dict result. Tracked on backend-market-scanner-followups.
Non-blocking: test_ibkr_scanner.py covers not_authenticated for GET /api/ibkr/scanner/params but not for POST /api/ibkr/scanner/run. Tracked on backend-market-scanner-followups.

review.notes: Tests/coverage: backend 959 passed, 99.94% coverage; frontend 700 passed, 99.7%+ coverage (both well above the 90% gate). Static analysis (ruff/mypy, eslint/tsc) clean on both sides. openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts regenerated and verified to match the committed snapshot exactly. The rate-limit-as-429 vs unavailable-as-200 distinction this task's context flagged as worth double-checking is correctly implemented and tested. No test attempts a live gateway call; FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED defaults to false throughout. No UI surface (backend-only change) -- browser walkthrough and e2e suite don't apply. The checklist's 'decide X' item has a matching decisions entry. One blocking correctness bug found via code-review pass + manual reproduction (see comments) -- needs a fix and a regression test before re-review.
